posts.author: conandaily.com@conandaily.com
posts.text:
Jalen Hurts placed on IR with blood clots amid battle over medical protocols

Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 National Football League season after being diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli—severe blood clots located in his lungs. The serious medical situation has sparked a major controversy regarding player safety, medical protocols, and institutional transparency within the league.The timeline of the issue began when Hurts sustained a calf injury during a recent matchup against the Los Angeles Rams after getting cleated. After reporting discomfort, medical evaluations revealed a superficial blood clot. Despite the diagnosis, specialists in London, England, United Kingdom—where the Eagles traveled to play the Jacksonville Jaguars—cleared him to play, concluding that activity and mobility were safe. He subsequently played in the international game and flew back with the team. However, subsequent ultrasounds and extensive testing revealed that the clot had shifted, ultimately leading to the discovery of multiple clots in his lungs. He has since been placed on injured reserve (IR) and started on blood thinners, which sideline him from all football activities.In response to public and media backlash, NFL chief medical officer Dr. Allen Sills defended the handling of the situation. He stated that the medical staff demonstrated incredible vigilance, utilized state-of-the-art imaging, and prioritized conservative, cautious care. The league maintained that all decisions were driven by medical prudence rather than external or football-related pressures, asserting that accusations of putting players in harm’s way are unfounded.Conversely, the National Football League Players Association (NFLPA) has strongly pushed back, calling for a comprehensive and independent investigation into the medical care provided to Hurts. The union criticized the league for hastily concluding that the team acted appropriately without conducting a proper, transparent inquiry. Highlighting that establishing the exact facts is vital to safeguarding player health moving forward, the NFLPA remains at odds with league officials over accountability and the oversight of complex medical clearances.Born in Houston, Texas, United States, Hurts turned 28 on August 7, 2026. He is 6’1″ tall.In April 2020, Hurts was selected 53rd overall by the Philadelphia Eagles in the second round of the 2020 NFL draft. In May 2023, he graduated from the University of Oklahoma in in Norman, Oklahoma, USA with a master’s degree in human relations.https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XX0hmmX4ycI

Mayfield will need to regain strength after Sunday’s dislocation and likely will miss some time. But good news overall.

posts.author: tompelissero.bsky.social
posts.text:
By trading J.J. McCarthy now, the Vikings save over $4.6M in cash and cap space and get an unconditional fifth-round pick in the next draft that, depending how the Giants finish, could end up being a top-150 selection.

Meanwhile, New York adds another former first-round pick QB.

posts.author: tompelissero.bsky.social
posts.text:
Trade! The Vikings are sending QB J.J. McCarthy to the Giants for a 2027 fifth-round pick, sources tell The Ringer and Netflix Sports.

With Jaxson Dart out for the regular season, New York adds another young QB, while Minnesota gains flexibility and McCarthy gets a fresh start.

posts.author: tompelissero.bsky.social
posts.text: The 49ers are signing veteran DT Naquan Jones off the Vikings practice squad, per source.

posts.author: tompelissero.bsky.social
posts.text: Giants QB Jaxson Dart is getting additional medical opinions on his injured knee that will determine whether to have surgery, which in turn will determine whether he can return this season or not. For now, he’s out indefinitely, as ESPN reported. Jameis Winston takes over as QB1.

posts.text: Sources: The #Seahawks are signing veteran QB Drew Lock, bringing him back to Seattle for a second stint. He will backup Sam Darnold.

posts.text:
Sources: Colorado QB Shedeur Sanders is scheduled to visit the #Raiders early next week. 

Las Vegas holds the No. 6 pick in the draft. They have been doing work on QBs and have other QB prospects also coming into their building.

posts.text:
Former #Bucs OC Byron Leftwich is back in coaching as he is joining Deion Sanders’ staff at Colorado.

Leftwich interviewed for multiple NFL jobs this past cycle (Pats HC, Seahawks OC) but now makes the move to college.

Harrison Hand biography: 13 things about footballer born in Cherry Hill, New Jersey

Harrison Hand is an American football cornerback born in Cherry Hill, New Jersey, United States. His cousins Turk McBride and Antwine Perez are former football players. Hand is Denise Peterson‘s son. He has two sisters namely Benaiah Hand and Brianna Hand.Harrison 5’11” tall and is registered weight is 185 pounds. Here are 13 more things about him:From 2017 to 2018, he played football at Baylor University in Waco, Texas, USA.In 2019, he played football at Temple University in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA.In April 2020, he was drafted in the fifth round of the National Football League draft by the Minnesota Vikings. On April 3, 2021, he hosted a youth workout session at Adrenaline Sports Performance and Training in Cherry Hill.On August 23, 2022, the Minnesota Vikings waived him. On August 24, 2022, the New York Giants claimed him off waivers.On August 30, 2022, the New York Giants waived him.On August 31, 2022, the New York Giants signed him to the practice squad.On September 5, 2022, the New York Giants released him.On September 13, 2022, he was signed to the practice squad of the Chicago Bears.On December 22, 2022, he was promoted to the active roster of the Chicago Bears.
